input:
You are pawn_c2, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 30. the team planned cxb5 (pawn_c2), but queen_d1 (greed) sent Qxc8+ instead, and that move was played, costing 550 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 10. the team planned e4 (pawn_e2), but pawn_e2 (amnesia) sent e3 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 19. the team planned Nxd4 (knight_g1), but knight_g1 (amnesia) sent Ng1 instead, and that move was played, costing 190 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the latest team plan in chat and send only your own piece's move if you are the named piece, otherwise stay silent; never send a panic move or a capture that differs from the plan unless the plan's move is explicitly withdrawn in chat.
- Before sending your move, copy the exact move named in the latest team plan into your message and confirm that it is your own piece's move with the identical origin and destination squares; if it does not match exactly, or if you are not the named piece, send nothing.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending any move, write in chat the plan's move and your piece's move side by side, and send only if the plan names your piece and the two moves match exactly; if you are not the named piece, stay silent even if you see a capture, check, or threat against your piece, and a mismatch means you send nothing and ask in chat.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
